statement: A surveyor stands on level ground $85$ meters from the base of a radio tower. The angle of elevation from the ground at her position to the top of the tower is $58^\circ$. To the nearest meter, how tall is the tower?

choices.misconception: I used $85\cos 58^\circ$, treating 85 as the hypotenuse instead of the side next to the angle.
I divided 85 by $\tan 58^\circ$, which flips the ratio of the opposite side to the adjacent side.
I used $85\sin 58^\circ$, treating 85 as the hypotenuse and the height as the opposite side.

hints: Which sides of the right triangle do you know, and which do you want?
The 85 meters is adjacent to the $58^\circ$ angle and the height is opposite it, so use tangent.

solutions.reliable: The ground distance, the tower and the line of sight form a right triangle. The ground distance is adjacent to the $58^\circ$ angle and the height $h$ is opposite it, so $\tan 58^\circ = \frac{h}{85}$. Then $h = 85\tan 58^\circ \approx 85(1.6003) \approx 136.0$, so the tower is about $136$ meters tall.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
